prompt:
A cinematic storyboard sheet for a Sri Lankan television drama: 9 photorealistic film stills of ONE scene, laid out in a grid 3 panels across and 3 down, read left to right, then top to bottom. Every panel is a tall portrait 9:16 still of the same size, separated by thin, even, plain white gutters. All panels are the same scene's world, painted together: the same people, props, light and colour grade in every panel. The weather and the ground (dry or wet, rain falling or not) are as each panel says: they can change during the scene, and a panel that says it is dry has no rain and no wet ground.

Reference images, in order: image 1 is the location plate for Modern Hotel Operations Office; image 2 is the reference sheet for ChatGPT; image 3 is the reference sheet for orchestrator එක. Take from image 1: the kind of place: its ground, water, plants, structures and materials. It is ONE view of the place; each panel has its own camera position, so do not repeat this view in every panel; image 2: ChatGPT exactly as shown; image 3: orchestrator එක exactly as shown.

People (every panel): every person is a smooth, matte, faceless artist's mannequin in one solid colour, with jointed limbs and simple hands: Company A Operations Manager (Employee) is the red mannequin; Company B Operations Manager is the blue mannequin. A small raised ridge on the front of the head, where a nose would be, shows which way the head faces. Each mannequin has the person's real height and build and sits, stands and holds things exactly as a real person would. No faces, no hair, no clothes, no skin: only the mannequin colour. Everything else (the place, the props, the light, the weather) is a real, photorealistic film still.

World (every panel): Paint one cohesive storyboard sheet, four columns by three rows, with ten panels ordered left to right and top to bottom; leave the final two cells empty and unframed. Use smooth colour-coded artist's mannequins: Company B Operations Manager is blue, medium-tall and lean; Company A Operations Manager is red, medium-height with an average build. People are represented only through body pose and head direction. Render the office and props realistically: cream walls, pale oak furniture, dark task chairs, flush timber cupboards, glazed partitions and a matte-black widescreen desktop computer with a compact keyboard and mouse. Steady dry daytime weather, soft daylight from the window at camera left, warm recessed ceiling lighting, warm-neutral 4800K balance, restrained ivory and honey colours, and clean midtones remain consistent. Keep the office background slightly darker than the subjects. All software graphics are flat, using off-white, charcoal, grey and restrained teal. Draw no lettering, numerals, logos, captions, panel labels or arrows anywhere; represent interface information with unlettered blocks, bars and simple icons.

Geography: The action stays at one pale-oak workstation in the hotel office. The blue host stands at its left end facing screen right, and the red visitor stands at its right end facing screen left, with the monitor between them and its display angled into their shared viewing space. The room-side camera positions remain on the same side of their conversational axis. Looking inward from this side, the broad window and outdoor trees lie toward frame left, timber cupboards occupy the rear centre, and the glazed partition lies toward frame right. The host singles tighten toward the left end of the workstation; the visitor single tightens toward the right end. Screen inserts use a neutral, straight-on position directly in front of this same monitor, lower than the standing cameras. The monitor's narrow black bezel, a sliver of pale-oak desktop and a soft window-light strip at frame left connect the wider office views to these inserts; neither manager changes position.

PANEL 1 (row 1, column 1) — Standing head height, approximately 1.6 metres, looking inward across the room-side edge of the desk; waist-up two-shot, 35mm feel, medium depth of field. Background: The broad window and green trees are frame left, flush oak cupboards are behind the workstation at centre, and the glazed partition is frame right. Dark task chairs sit behind the pale-oak desk. The blue mannequin stands frame left with its chest facing screen right and its head turned three-quarter toward the red mannequin. Its near-side left hand extends toward screen right above the desk with the palm open upward, while its far-side right hand hangs empty beside its body. The red mannequin stands frame right with its chest facing screen left and its head turned three-quarter toward the host; both empty hands hang beside its body, with its right hand on the near side toward the camera. Between them, the black monitor shows a pale, simple interface without an enquiry card or workflow diagram, with the keyboard and mouse resting on the desk below.
PANEL 2 (row 1, column 2) — Standing head height, approximately 1.6 metres, from the room side of the axis; chest-up medium close-up with a 65mm feel and gently softened background. Background: A soft strip of the broad window remains at frame left, with the timber cupboard surfaces behind the blue mannequin toward centre-right. The same monitor bezel enters along the lower-right edge. The blue mannequin occupies the left portion of the panel, chest facing screen right and head turned three-quarter toward the visitor off frame right. Both hands are below the lower crop, and the shoulders remain upright beside the workstation. The narrow black monitor edge occupies the lower-right corner without revealing its display.
PANEL 3 (row 1, column 3) — Neutral-axis position directly in front of the same monitor, at display-centre height of approximately 1.2 metres; straight-on insert, 65mm feel, sharp across the display. Background: The monitor nearly fills the panel; a narrow blurred strip of window light remains at frame left, with a soft cream-and-oak background at frame right and a thin desktop strip below. The hotel management interface fills the monitor within its narrow matte-black bezel, with a slim navigation column at screen left and a broad pale workspace to its right. Small grey blocks indicate existing interface controls, while the main workspace remains open without an incoming enquiry card. No people or hands enter the frame.
PANEL 4 (row 2, column 1) — Exactly the screen-insert position used in shot 3, at approximately 1.2 metres; straight-on insert, 65mm feel, sharp across the display. Background: The same narrow window-light strip stays at frame left, the blurred cream-and-oak office remains frame right, and pale oak appears beneath the black bezel. The same hotel management interface now contains a large received-enquiry card centred in its pale workspace. The card has a broad grey heading block, two compact information chips and three neatly separated service rows indicated by simple icons and unlettered bars. The surrounding interface remains plain, without a central workflow hub or agent tiles.
PANEL 5 (row 2, column 2) — Return to the host's standing head-height position, approximately 1.6 metres, on the room side of the axis; chest-up medium close-up, 65mm feel. Background: The broad window remains a softened strip at frame left, timber cupboards occupy the background toward centre-right, and the monitor bezel stays at the lower-right edge. The blue mannequin stands at frame left with its chest facing screen right and its head held three-quarter toward the visitor off frame right. Its shoulders are level, and both hands remain below the lower crop. Only the narrow black edge of the computer enters at lower right; its display is outside the frame.
PANEL 6 (row 2, column 3) — Return to the identical neutral-axis display position, approximately 1.2 metres high; straight-on insert, 65mm feel, sharp across the display. Background: The black bezel encloses nearly the whole panel, with the same blurred window-light strip at frame left, cream-and-oak background at frame right and pale desktop below. An off-white dashboard fills the screen, with a large charcoal circular hub edged by a thin teal rim and a soft teal halo. Four thin grey connectors lead to four unlit ivory tiles arranged upper left, upper right, lower left and lower right around the hub; their icons are a speech bubble, an unnumbered calendar grid, a checklist and a calculator with blank buttons. Every tile has a grey border, and the lower dashboard band remains empty.
PANEL 7 (row 3, column 1) — Same standing head-height host setup, approximately 1.6 metres, retaining the conversational axis; chest-up medium close-up, 65mm feel. Background: The softened window strip remains frame left, timber cupboards remain behind the blue mannequin toward centre-right, and the black monitor bezel remains lower right. The blue mannequin occupies frame left, standing upright with its chest directed screen right and its head turned three-quarter toward the visitor off frame right. Both hands remain below the lower crop, with neither arm reaching toward the computer. The monitor is represented only by its narrow black edge at the bottom right.
PANEL 8 (row 3, column 2) — Same neutral-axis screen-insert position at approximately 1.2 metres; straight-on insert, 65mm feel, sharp across the display. Background: The same narrow bezel surrounds the screen, with soft window light at frame left, blurred cream-and-oak office at frame right and a slim pale-oak desktop strip below. The circular charcoal hub and all four surrounding agent tiles retain their previous positions, now with teal illuminated borders and clearly visible connectors. A lower row of four pale-grey system cards is connected to the workflow, carrying simple document-stack, checked-document, contact-record and hotel-building icons without lettering. The connected workflow fills the screen unobstructed, with no quotation sheet or amber status badge.
PANEL 9 (row 3, column 3) — Same standing head-height host setup, approximately 1.6 metres, from the room side of the axis; chest-up medium close-up, 65mm feel. Background: The window-light strip remains at frame left, soft timber cupboard surfaces remain centre-right, and the same monitor bezel enters at lower right. The blue mannequin stands frame left with its chest facing screen right and its head held three-quarter toward the visitor off frame right. Its torso remains upright and both hands stay below the lower crop. The black computer edge remains at the lower-right corner, with the display itself outside the frame.

Bodies (every panel): each person sits or stands the way a real person does the task in front of them, never posed for the camera. The body faces the task and only the head turns: someone at a steering wheel sits squarely behind it, the wheel centred in front of the chest, back against the seat, both hands on the rim; someone at a desk sits square to it; someone at a stove faces the stove. A camera beside a person sees the body side-on, not the chest. Nobody looks into or faces the lens unless the panel says so. Head and eyes turn together: the eyes never roll hard to one side while the face points at the camera; a near-frontal face looks just past the lens.

Draw NO text of any kind: no panel numbers, no captions, no titles, no timestamps, no arrows, no labels, no borders other than the gutters. The people, place and everyday details are Sri Lankan.
